A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same retrieval-problem study, and their text, equations, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. Appendices A-C are retained, while v2 adds Appendix D.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLM benchmarking, transformer-training experiments, circuit ablations, and attention-emergence measurements in Sections 4 and 7-9 and Appendices B-C.

after.justification: V2 retains original LLM accuracies, training results, circuit-validation outcomes, and attention-emergence measurements, including results documented in Appendices B-D.

M1.justification: The architectures, input construction, IC/non-IC objectives, and reconstructed retrieval mechanisms are retained. The written IC target dimension changes from DK to DN, but both versions set N = K = 4 and specify the same token concatenation; this does not establish a model change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic retrieval task and the equations, lives-with, kingdoms, functions, and relatives formulations. The added D = 1 point extends the existing difficulty sweep without introducing a new dataset or task family.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama 3.1 405b, and random guessing. The IC/non-IC comparison is also retained; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Figure 2 extends the evaluated difficulty range from D = 2-13 to D = 1-13. Appendix D also revises the reported ablation unit from useful heads to individual attention paths, without establishing whether experiments were rerun. Other stated training budgets, metrics, sample sizes, and prompting procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix D explicitly reports testing individual attention paths for circuit nonredundancy, refining v1 Section 8.2's whole-head ablation account. The curriculum/depth analyses, reconstructed circuits, appendix attention maps, and emergence traces are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report eight training runs per layer and formulation, average results across those runs, and average final validation loss over the last 100 steps. Neither adds seed disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars.

E6.justification: Figure 2 adds 100% accuracy at D = 1 for all four LLMs; their D = 2-13 values are unchanged. Section 9.2 changes the reported induction-head emergence time from 400 to 450 epochs. Appendix D refines the first-useful-layer ablation error from below 0.1 to 0.05-0.1; the other principal results are retained.

T1.justification: Section 5 adds an independence-based lemma and proof establishing the shared-token-or-position condition that v1 directly assumed. The main contiguous-information argument and the log3(2D) depth lower bound remain unchanged, making this a limited revision of the theoretical support.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain the retrieval tasks, depth requirement, LLM success without fine-tuning, and curriculum-dependent sequential emergence of retrieval heads. V2 highlights logarithmic depth scaling in its abstract and contribution section, but that bound already appears in v1 Section 5; the conclusion retains the same substantive claims.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1's assertion that retrieval could not explicitly occur in training data because the task had not previously been stated. Section 10.2 develops the natural-language curriculum hypothesis through diversity of task difficulty. The limitations concerning generalization to LLMs and incomplete understanding of training dynamics are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D expands the previously brief circuit-reconstruction description into six steps, including inspection across prompts, iterative mechanism selection using validation loss below 0.05, and combined validation. This supplies additional reproducibility information about the existing analysis without establishing a newly implemented method.

R1.justification: V2 adds Chan et al. (2022) and connects its work on data-distribution properties and emergent in-context learning to the curriculum discussion. The remaining cited works and related-work positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: contributions receive a separate section, related work moves from Section 2 to Section 11, natural-language motivation moves earlier, and circuit-validation details move into Appendix D. The abstract, theoretical exposition, and discussion are also rewritten or expanded.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves below the abstract, Figure 2 extends its horizontal axis to D = 1, and Figure 3 replaces letter labels with indexed tokens. V1 Figure 6's attention-map display is removed from the main text, but its maps remain in Appendix B. Other figures are relocated or renumbered with their graphical content retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves procedural transparency through Appendix D and makes the narrative and formal setup easier to follow. The 450-epoch correction also aligns the prose with the retained emergence figure. These limited gains outweigh the new DN-for-DK target-dimension inconsistency; the principal experimental evidence, depth bound, and acknowledged limitations remain essentially unchanged.
